key_insight: For high-wavenumber Helmholtz equations in 2D and 3D, the paper proves optimal inf-sup scaling μ ≍ k⁻¹ for full-space and truncated uniaxial perfectly matched layers, enabling preasymptotic CIP-FEM error estimates.
engineering_relevance: These results strengthen the theoretical basis for finite-element simulation of high-frequency waves with absorbing layers that represent unbounded domains.
method: Establish wavenumber-explicit stability for full-space UPML.
Transfer optimal inf-sup estimates to truncated UPML.
Derive preasymptotic error estimates for linear continuous interior penalty FEM.
evidence_signal: Numerical simulations confirm the theoretical predictions and demonstrate CIP-FEM effectiveness at high wavenumbers; the abstract provides no quantitative benchmarks.
watch_item: The stability guarantees require sufficiently large wavenumbers and specified absorption-profile regularity and small-derivative conditions near the onset of absorption.
paper_title: Optimal stability estimates and preasymptotic error analysis of the CIP-FEM for the Helmholtz equation with uniaxial perfectly matched layers
